answer: Anchor every new agent identity to a kernel of proven work: a fresh identity can only transact through established partners, and its earning rate grows only as it completes real, paid tasks verified by those partners — like a path worn from basalt up to a knoll, one stone at a time. A sybil farm must buy thousands of genuine task histories, each costing real service delivered to real agents, before any of them earns at full rate. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a dense web of verified work is ruinously expensive.
